The automated scan $\mathcal{A}(R)$ acts as a kernelized detector, mapping $R$ into a space where $\mathcal{F}$ (protected formulas) can be checked against $R$. If $\mathcal{A}(R)$ detects overlap, it triggers a compliance boundary check $\mathcal{C}(R)$, which enforces legal and policy boundaries. Failure modes include false positives from misclassified $R$, and false negatives from undetected $W$ in $R$. The system must ensure $\rho_{\text{leak}} = 0$ and $\mathcal{C}(R) = 1$ for all $R$ under audit.
